_about: Forecast/history point per town. gauge = OPW waterlevel.ie station on the town's named river (CC BY 4.0). point = coordinate sent to Open-Meteo; shifted from the gauge only where the gauge cell returned a different, minor stream (see FLAGS-LOG F1).

towns.shiftReason: Gauge cell returned ~0.3 m³/s (a minor stream); the Blackwater cell 7 km downstream returns ~24 m³/s, above Mallow upstream as expected.
Gauge cell returned ~0.2 m³/s; the best cell within 5 km returns ~5.5 m³/s.
towns.caveat: The model's 10-year mean (8.7 m³/s) is about 58% of the published ~15 m³/s for the Bandon; the global model under-resolves this small catchment. Levels compare the forecast with this point's own history, so they stay consistent, but don't compare the m³/s with local gauges.

The model's 10-year mean (13.5 m³/s) is about a third of the ~37 m³/s long-term figure quoted for the Slaney (secondary source). No nearby cell did better. Levels compare the forecast with this point's own history.

towns.shiftReason: Gauge cell returned ~3 m³/s (a side stream). The model's Fergus runs through the cells west of town (6.4 → 9.0 → 12.4 → 13.5 → 17.2 m³/s going downstream, 2025 means); the cell just below Ennis averages ~13.5 m³/s, in line with the Fergus (~25.7 m³/s at its mouth).
Gauge cell returned ~0.5 m³/s (a drain, not the Shannon); the cell 3 km west returns ~44 m³/s, more than Carrick-on-Shannon upstream as expected.
towns.caveat: The model's 10-year mean (76 m³/s) is about 78% of the ~98 m³/s published for the Shannon at Athlone weir. The gauge's own cell picked up a drain, so the point was moved 3 km west onto the main channel.
